claims.statement: EHDS includes health data generated by medical devices and wellness applications among categories relevant to governed secondary use.
EU medical-device rules govern clinical investigations and software or devices with medical intended purposes, making intended use and study design material dependencies.

EHDS secondary-use access is permit-based, may carry proportionate fees, occurs in a secure processing environment and can be refused where serious intellectual-property or trade-secret risk cannot be satisfactorily addressed.

EHDS Chapter IV generally starts applying in March 2029, while its mandatory availability rules for clinical-study and research-cohort data apply from March 2031, so it is not a near-term clinic-data shortcut.
In Poland, device clinical investigations under MDR Articles 62 or 82 require a positive bioethics opinion and URPL authorisation; the exact route depends on the device and protocol.
Established providers already sell end-to-end wearable CRO services, device platforms, analytical and clinical validation, regulatory support, signal quality control and participant operations.

The proposed 2-4 founder-hours per day is plausible only if a qualified principal investigator, clinic coordinator and privacy or quality owner accept the participant-facing and regulated work; those commitments are not yet evidenced.

contrary_evidence: EHDS imposes governance and purpose limits; it does not make clinic data freely licensable or remove MDR clinical-investigation requirements.
EHDS mandatory secondary-use access for clinical studies and research cohorts is phased to 2031, outside the near-term validation period.
VivoSense, Empatica, TNO and Delve already cover large parts of the proposed protocol, device, analytics, regulatory and participant-support stack.
Polish device studies can require both bioethics approval and URPL authorisation, and medical-experiment governance depends on qualified clinical leadership.

economics.acquisition_route: Research update: partner occupational-medicine and sleep clinics for collection and sell to European wearable, digital-health and medical-device teams. Incumbents already sell end-to-end wearable CRO and validation services, so the unvalidated acquisition wedge must be a specific protocol, Central-European cohort, faster sponsored pilot or materially lower cost rather than generic wearable validation.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: complete 3 paid studies by year 2, reach 5 million PLN annual revenue by year 5, build 4 million PLN founder equity and retained cash by year 7, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-11. No public evidence validates sponsor count, pricing, renewal or valuation assumptions.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated: 2-4 hours per day only if a qualified principal investigator, clinic coordinator and privacy or quality owner accept participant, safety, consent, documentation and study-operations responsibility.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 40%-70% after clinic, participant, equipment, secure-compute, insurance, regulatory and biostatistics costs; no public competitor pricing or clinic-cost quote was found.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 18-36 months; the first governed protocol may require bioethics, URPL, insurance and sponsor documentation before reusable benchmark economics can be tested.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 80,000-300,000 PLN per validation project and 50,000-200,000 PLN annual benchmark access. Incumbents demonstrate a paid category but do not publish comparable project prices.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat may follow device versions, endpoints and new intended uses, but no sponsor renewal or benchmark-license evidence exists.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Every protocol run expands normative ranges, failure modes and cross-device comparability
fingerprint.customer: European biosensor, wearable and digital-health product teams needing independent human validation
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Repeat clinic capacity on supply and device-development partnerships on demand
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Clinic-executed protocol, statistical validation and controlled derived-data access
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A sponsor pays on study milestones and for governed benchmark access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new device or algorithm version needs credible comparison against a stable protocol and clinician labels

founder_fit: Uses the founder's EEG, neuroscience and data-science background.
Clinic staff can own participant contact.
Creates a reusable evidence asset rather than hourly consulting alone.

The 175,000 PLN starting-capital estimate exceeds the founder's approximately 100,000 PLN free capital, so a sponsor-funded pilot, staged protocol or unusually strong case for family capital is required.
risks: Participant harm, privacy breach or invalid consent.
Sponsors may prefer established contract research organisations.
EHDS timing and permit rules do not confer near-term or exclusive rights to clinic data.
A study can cross from low-risk benchmarking into a regulated clinical investigation based on intended purpose and protocol design.
The founder cannot personally substitute for required qualified clinical leadership while retaining a full-time job.

structure.commercial_archetype: Clinical data foundry and validation service
structure.control_point: Exclusive execution rights for a standard protocol at partner clinics and licensed rights to governed derived benchmarks
structure.critical_dependency: Ethics approval, informed consent or another valid legal basis, clinical partners, device-regulatory boundaries and representative recruitment

thesis: Run standardised, ethics-approved EEG, wearable and sleep or fatigue validation protocols through contracted clinics, then sell device makers reproducible benchmark analyses and permitted derived datasets. Clinic channels, protocol consistency and paired clinician labels form a defensible validation asset distinct from a consumer wellness app.
title: Clinic-Bound Biosignal Validation Foundry
uncertainties: Exact regulatory classification by protocol and intended use
Sponsor willingness to license a Central-European benchmark
Whether a sponsor-funded first protocol can keep founder cash exposure below available free capital
Whether derived-benchmark rights survive clinic, sponsor, participant-consent, GDPR and EHDS constraints
Publicly unobserved project pricing and renewal rates versus established wearable CROs
